You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 17 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17, has left education or training and been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child or children you're inquiring about:**

1. **How old is your child?** (If you have multiple children, we can go through them one at a time)

The eligibility criteria differ based on age:
- Children **under 16** generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** typically don't qualify

Please tell me the age(s) of the child/children you're asking about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 17 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), his eligibility will depend on whether he's in approved education or training.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to know about Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently:**
- **In approved education or training?** (such as school, college, or an approved training course), OR
- **Has he recently left education or training?** (within the last 20 weeks)

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's recently left education actually. He's been registered with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for letting me know. So Alex has recently left education and is registered with the local careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - there's a potential 20-week extension period for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education and registered with certain services.

**To determine if Alex qualifies for this extension, I need to know:**

1. **How long ago did Alex leave education?** (I need to check if it's been less than 20 weeks)
2. **Which careers service is he registered with?** (The extension applies if registered with a government careers service, Connexions, or the armed services)

The extension can last up to 20 weeks from when he left education, or until he turns 18, whichever comes first.

Can you tell me approximately when Alex left education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been less than 20 weeks - just a couple of months ago actually. And yes, he's registered with the government careers service to help him work out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex left education just a couple of months ago (which is within the 20-week period) and he's registered with the government careers service. This means he may qualify for the extension period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

For young people aged 16+, if they work 24 hours or more per week and aren't in approved education or training, they wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

What's Alex's current work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all at the moment. He's just been focusing on working with the careers service to figure out what direction he wants to go in.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not working at all, which means he meets this requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** 

Specifically, I need to know if he's receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in his own name (not as part of your household claim)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?**

This is important because different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- **All English apprenticeships** would disqualify him
- **Scottish Modern Apprenticeships** would disqualify him
- **Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships** are approved (so he would still qualify)
- **Other Welsh apprenticeships** would disqualify him

Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just registered with the careers service at the moment working out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**, OR
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
3. **You have pre-settled status** and are:
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold, OR
   - Actively seeking work (up to 91 days), OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family (and not claiming certain benefits), OR
   - Studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - Are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside, OR
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** or living in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to confirm you have responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned he lives at home with you, so it sounds like you meet the "living with the child" requirement. To confirm:

**Do you live with Alex?**

(Note: You can also qualify if you contribute to his upkeep or pay maintenance, but living together is the most straightforward way to meet this requirement.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another guardian or relative
- Anyone else who might have a claim

If someone else is claiming, only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child (though it's possible to transfer the claim if both parties agree).

Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following describes Alex's current living situation?**

- Is he **in hospital**?
- Is he **in local authority care**?
- Is he **in a foster care arrangement**?
- Or is he **living normally at home with you** (not in any of the above situations)?

You mentioned he lives at home with you, so I assume it's the last option, but I want to confirm there are no special circumstances like a hospital stay or care arrangement.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's just living normally at home with me. None of those other situations apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Just one final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you receiving any payments from the local council specifically for Alex's care, accommodation, or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me now provide you with the final assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

Based on all the information you've provided, you meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex.

### Why You Qualify:

Alex qualifies under the **20-week extension period** for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education. Specifically:

✅ Alex is 17 years old  
✅ He left education within the last 20 weeks (about 2 months ago)  
✅ He's registered with the government careers service  
✅ He's not working 24+ hours per week  
✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right  
✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✅ You normally live in the UK  
✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him  
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him  
✅ The local council isn't paying towards his care  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware**: If you or your partner earn over £60,000, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply (though you can still claim)
5. **Payments**: Made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Important Note About the Extension:

Remember that this 20-week extension period will end either:
- 20 weeks after Alex left education, OR
- When Alex turns 18, **whichever comes sooner**

So it's important to apply soon to maximize the benefit period!

**To apply, visit:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about the application process or your eligibility?
